stem.text: There are several different human blood group systems.
Each blood group system is based on the presence or absence of certain antigens attached to the cell surface membranes of red blood cells.
In the ABO blood group system, the ABO gene, known as gene I, has three alleles. The gene is located on an autosome.

items: Allele IA codes for an enzyme that adds antigen A to the cell surface membrane.
Allele IB codes for an enzyme that adds antigen B to the cell surface membrane.
Allele IO codes for a non-functional enzyme, so no antigen is added.

stem.text: Explain what is meant by the term recessive and the term codominant.

points.text:
recessive
phenotype of (recessive) allele is masked by a dominant allele
or
two copies of the (recessive) allele are needed for phenotype (to be displayed)
or
alleles only affect the phenotype in the absence of a dominant allele
or
(genotype) must be homozygous for the (recessive) allele to affect the phenotype ;

codominant
both alleles affect the phenotype (in the heterozygote) ;

explanation.text: Dominance concerns how alleles are expressed in a heterozygote. A recessive allele is masked by a dominant one, whereas codominant alleles both contribute to the phenotype.

reasoningChain: Define recessive using the heterozygous state.
Define codominance as expression of both alleles.

explanation.text: ABO phenotypes depend on two alleles in each individual even though three alleles exist in the population. A and B can each be homozygous or carry the recessive O allele; AB expresses both codominant alleles.

reasoningChain: List both genotypes for A and B.
Give the single genotype for AB and for O.

stem.text: In the Rhesus blood group system, a gene codes for a protein known as the Rhesus factor. This protein is an antigen found on the surface of red blood cells.

items: The dominant allele D codes for the Rhesus factor.
The recessive allele d results in no Rhesus factor.
A person who has the Rhesus factor is described as Rhesus positive (Rh+).
A person who lacks the Rhesus factor is described as Rhesus negative (Rh–).
The gene coding for the Rhesus factor is on a different autosome from the ABO gene.

stem.text: Complete the Punnett square in Figure 5.1 to show the possible blood groups of children from these parents.

items: Parent 1 is heterozygous for blood group B and heterozygous for the Rhesus factor.
Parent 2 has blood group O and is heterozygous for the Rhesus factor.
